Subject Communication dated 19-7-38 from the Netherlands Consulate-General
concerning L. Kalivoda and members of his orchestra.
Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by [手写签名]

Enquiries show that L. Kalivoda arrived in Shang-
hai from Harbin in March, 1937 together with 9 members of his
orchestra, Messrs: E. NESSWETHA, G. ROSENBERG, F. HUDEC, J.
JOZIFEK, J. TAUCHMANN, C. NOVOTNY, F. MARSHIK, V. JANISH and
F. PRUDIL. Here they were employed at the restaurant Arcadia,
291 Rue Amiral Courbet, until April, 1938, after which they
returned to Harbin.

While in Shanghai they did not come to the notice
of the Municipal Police in connection with any activities of
an undesirable character.

With regard to Adolf VATNER, it appears that this
individual joined the orchestra in question only very recently.
His name is not known to the manager of the restaurant Arcadia
nor to Messrs S.S. Nenishkis and J.A. Zabulanis, Honorary
President and President of the Lithuanian Association in Shang-
hai, respectively. In all probability, he is identical with
a certain Adolf A. VATNER, Lithuanian, born in 1914 who accord-
ing to the French Police Boarding House Section, arrived in
Shanghai from Harbin on 17-3-32. Later he resided at various
addresses in the Settlement and French Concession and on
different occasions described himself as a pharmaceutist,
merchant, or manager of the Vienna Garden. It is reported
that on 15-11-36 he absconded from a licenced boarding house
at 7/133 Baikal Road leaving an unpaid bill of $115.00. for
boarding and lodging. Attached herewith is a copy of an
article which appeared in the CHINA PRESS of 2-5-37. It appears
from this article that Adolf Vanter was sentenced to 2 months
imprisonment or $100 fine by the Hongkong Court in April, 1937

报告
日期：1938年7月23日。
事由：荷兰总领事馆1938年7月19日来函，涉及L. Kalivoda及其乐团成员。
撰写人：侦探副督察普罗科菲耶夫（Prokofiev）。转发人：[手写签名]

经查，L. Kalivoda于1937年3月与其乐团的9名成员从哈尔滨抵达上海，
成员包括：E. NESSWETHA、G. ROSENBERG、F. HUDEC、J.
JOZIFEK、J. TAUCHMANN、C. NOVOTNY、F. MARSHIK、V. JANISH 和
F. PRUDIL诸先生。他们在亚尔培路（Rue Amiral Courbet）291号的阿卡迪亚餐厅（Arcadia restaurant）受雇，直至1938年4月，随后返回哈尔滨。

在上海期间，他们并未因任何不良性质的活动引起工部局警务处的注意。

关于阿道夫·瓦特纳（Adolf VATNER），此人似乎只是最近才加入该乐团。
阿卡迪亚餐厅经理以及上海立陶宛协会名誉主席S.S. Nenishkis先生和主席J.A. Zabulanis先生均不知晓其名。他很可能与某位阿道夫·A·瓦特纳（Adolf A. VATNER）为同一人，该人为立陶宛籍，生于1914年，据法租界巡捕房寄宿管理处记载，于1932年3月17日从哈尔滨抵达上海。此后他居住在租界及法租界的多个地址，并曾自称药剂师、商人或维也纳花园（Vienna Garden）经理。据报道，1936年11月15日，他从贝加尔路（Baikal Road）7/133号的一家持牌寄宿寓所潜逃，留下未付的食宿费115.00美元。随函附上1937年5月2日《字林西报》（CHINA PRESS）刊登的一篇文章副本。从该文章看来，阿道夫·范特（Adolf Vanter）于1937年4月被香港法院判处两个月监禁或罚款100美元，

The CHINA PRESS, Sunday, May 2, 1937

GENERAL STOWAWAYS
Paying for drinks in bar of Pres. Coolidge is giveaway.
JAILED IN COLONY

Stowaways on Pacific boats, particularly on the Orient end,
are becoming more of a nuisance every day. Last Sunday the SHIP-
PING GREEN reported two men in Hongkong who had stowed away on
the President Harrison and caught by the Hongkong Police. Now
comes another report from the Colony of three men charged in the
Hongkong Court with stowing away on the President Coolidge.

The three men, Adolf VATNER, 23, a Lithuanian, Sergei KURZANOFF,
29, and Eugene DENISSOFF, 24, both Russians, was charged before
Mr. K. Keen at the Central Magistracy with stowing away on the
Coolidge from Hongkong to Manila and with entering the Colony on
April 12 without a valid passport.

Detectives stated that the trio arrived in the Colony from Can-
ton on April 12. All three were fined $ 50 or one month on each
charge and expulsion orders were made against them.

Paying drinks is giveaway

According to the "Manila Bulletin", they were three of the most
distinguished-looking stowaways ever to see Manila from a ship's
porthole. Well dressed and apparently men of means, the three were
discovered on the liner while en route from Hongkong to Manila,
simply because they paid for their drinks in the lounge instead of
signing for them.

Anxious to visit Manila, they boarded the Coolidge at Hongkong
just before sailing time. The men easily passed as passengers.
En route to Manila they roamed about the first-class public rooms
and took drinks in the bar.

They made no efforts to conceal themselves from ship officers
and men . They acted naturally and showed no outward sign which
might give them away to ship officers. But they failed to reckon
with ship customs. They were calmly paying for what they drank,

《字林西报》，1937年5月2日，星期日

一般偷渡者
在柯立芝总统号酒吧付酒钱露了马脚。
在殖民地入狱

太平洋航线船只上的偷渡者，特别是在远东航段，日益成为麻烦。上周日，《航运绿报》（SHIPPING GREEN）报道了两名在香港偷乘哈里森总统号（President Harrison）并被香港警方抓获的男子。现在又有来自殖民地的报告称，三名男子被香港法院指控偷乘柯立芝总统号（President Coolidge）。

这三名男子，23岁的立陶宛人阿道夫·瓦特纳（Adolf VATNER），29岁的谢尔盖·库尔扎诺夫（Sergei KURZANOFF）和24岁的叶夫根尼·德尼索夫（Eugene DENISSOFF，均为俄罗斯人），在中央裁判司署由K. Keen先生审理，被控从香港至马尼拉途中偷乘柯立芝总统号，并于4月12日无有效护照进入殖民地。

侦探称，这三人于4月12日从广州抵达殖民地。三项指控每项均被罚款50美元或监禁一个月，并被下达驱逐令。

付酒钱露了马脚

据《马尼拉公报》（Manila Bulletin）称，他们是透过船舷窗看到马尼拉的最具风度的偷渡者。这三人衣着考究，看似富有，在从香港前往马尼拉的途中在邮轮上被发现，仅仅是因为他们在休息室喝酒时付了现金，而不是签单记账。

出于访问马尼拉的愿望，他们在开船前一刻于香港登上了柯立芝总统号。这些人轻易地伪装成了乘客。在前往马尼拉的途中，他们在头等舱公共区域闲逛，并在酒吧饮酒。

他们并未试图向船员隐瞒身份。他们举止自然，没有表现出任何可能向船员暴露身份的外在迹象。但他们未考虑到船上的惯例。他们平静地为所饮之物付款，

and passengers are usually allowed to sign chits for the drinks.
The steward began to watch them and in a few hours discovered
them to be stowaways. They were locked in a hospital room used for
violent patients. And there they remained during the ship's stay in
port. Two watchmen saw to it that they did not escape.
Posed as fireman
Bound for Manila, officers of the Coolidge turned over to
the police at Hongkong another stowaway, this one from Shanghai.
The stowaway, also a Russian, boarded the ship at Shanghai dressed in
the uniform of a fireman. He had a cap worn by members of a firemen's
union and in this manner escaped detection for some time. The first
officer saw him loitering around the boat deck and asked him what
he was doing there . He replied: "Will you tell your captain that I am
a stowaway?" "You could have struck me down with a feather"
the first officer recalled the incident. " Would I tell the captain?
Would I!"
On being informed of the presence of a stowaway on board, the
captain ordered him placed in the brig and handed over to the Hongkong
Police.

冒充司炉工
柯立芝总统号驶往马尼拉，船员将另一名来自上海的偷渡者移交给香港警方。这名偷渡者也是俄罗斯人，他在上海登船时身穿司炉工制服。他戴着一顶司炉工工会成员的帽子，以此方式逃避检查一段时间。大副看见他在艇甲板附近徘徊，便问他在做什么。他回答说：“你能告诉你的船长我是个偷渡者吗？”“你简直可以用一根羽毛把我打倒，”大副回忆此事时说。“我会告诉船长吗？我当然会！”
得知船上有一名偷渡者后，船长下令将其关入禁闭室，并移交给香港警方。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. ...
S.1, Special Branch STUBOX
REPORT
Date Nov. 12, 19 37.
Subject Communication from the Netherlands Consulate-General concerning
I. Waldhuter.
Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky. Forwarded by C Crawford S.I.

Izak Waldhuter, better known in Shanghai under his stage
name Isidor Alexeyevich Vlnogradoff, is a Polish citizen of
Jewish origin who was born on November 8, 1894, at Czartkov,
Galicia, Austria. He received his education in a Normal
School at Tarnopol and subsequently attended the Lvov
University (Pharmaceutical Faculty) for 9 months. He
served in the Austrian Army during the Great War from 1914
to 1916 when he was taken prisoner by the Russians. He
was detained in the Irkutsk Prisoners Camp, Siberia until
outbreak of the Revolution in Russia in 1917, after which he
was released and left for Vladivostok with a Jewish Theatrical
Company. In 1918 he proceeded to Harbin where he worked as
an impressario and artist until 1920 when he returned to
Vladivostok. From 1922 to 1924 he resided in Harbin working
in the same capacity after which he left for Chita, U.S.S.R.
with Volodin & Smolich's Opera Company. When in Chita,
Waldhuter received employment as an advance manager of the
Isedora Dunkan's Ballet Company with which he subsequently
visited Vladivostok and returned to Harbin. In 1931 and
in 1935 he visited Shanghai with Carpi's Opera and Italian
Opera Company respectively, as stage manager.

On March 28, 1937 Waldhuter arrived in Shanghai from
Harbin with Kalivoda's Symphonic Orchestra which he engaged
from Czecho-Slovaskia. From April 1, 1937 the above orchestra
has been employed with the Arcadia Ball Room, Rue Bourgeat.

He is registered with the local Polish Consulate-General
and resides at No.708 Rue Bourgeat with his wife, Mrs. E.N.
Waldhuter, nee Medvedchikova, and their daughter Margarita,
14 years of age.

报告
日期：1937年11月12日。
事由：荷兰总领事馆关于I. Waldhuter的来函。
撰写人：侦探副督察 Tcheremshansky。转发人：C Crawford S.I.

Izak Waldhuter，在上海以其艺名Isidor Alexeyevich Vlnogradoff更为人知，是一名波兰籍犹太人，1894年11月8日出生于奥地利加利西亚地区的Czartkov。他在Tarnopol的一所师范学校接受教育，随后在Lvov大学（药学系）就读9个月。他在第一次世界大战期间于1914年至1916年在奥军服役，期间被俄军俘虏。他被关押在西伯利亚的伊尔库茨克战俘营，直到1917年俄国革命爆发，之后获释并随一家犹太戏剧公司前往符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴）。1918年他前往哈尔滨，担任经理人兼艺术家，直至1920年返回符拉迪沃斯托克。1922年至1924年他居住在哈尔滨，从事相同工作，随后随Volodin & Smolich歌剧团前往苏联赤塔。在赤塔期间，Waldhuter受雇为Isedora Dunkan芭蕾舞团的先行经理，随后随团访问符拉迪沃斯托克并返回哈尔滨。1931年和1935年，他分别作为舞台监督随Carpi歌剧团和意大利歌剧团访问上海。

1937年3月28日，Waldhuter随Kalivoda交响乐团从哈尔滨抵达上海，该乐团是他从捷克斯洛伐克聘请的。自1937年4月1日起，上述乐团受雇于布尔热路（Rue Bourgeat）的阿卡迪亚舞厅。

他在当地波兰总领事馆注册，与妻子E.N. Waldhuter夫人（婚前姓Medvedchikova）及14岁的女儿Margarita居住在布尔热路708号。

Sir,

        I have the honour to inform you that Mr. Izak WALDHUTER,
has applied to this Consulate for a visé for admission into
the Netherlands Indies. Waldhuter is in possession of a
Polish passport, Serie I. No. 504114, No. 969/35, issued by the
Polish Consulate at Harbin, on September 3, 1935, valid
till September 3, 1938. According to his passport he was
born at Czertkov on November 8th 1894, and his profession
stated as Impresario and artist.
        He has been residing at Harbin for 16 years, whereas
he has been in Shanghai for the last 7 months.
        He intends to visit the Netherlands Indies in order to
arrange a contract for the band, which is employed at the
moment with the Arcadia Ballroom on Rue Bourgeat.
        Furthermore he stated to have his residence at 708
Rue Bourgeat.
        I should be much obliged to you if you would inform me,
if possible, whether anything is known against this person
from a political or moral point of view.
